label: Mailbox Chat
description: Durable mailbox relay that bridges chat networks (IRC, Discord, Slack, Matrix/Element, Telegram, WhatsApp, Mattermost, Viber, LINE, Discourse, and more) through per-adapter connectors. Every connected IRC channel or client -- and every other adapter's channel or client -- gets its own mailbox, so cross-adapter communication (an IRC channel talking to a Discord channel, say) flows through one shared, durable message store. While relaying, it also converts between each adapter's differing capabilities (formatting, attachments, threads, presence) so a message composed for one network still makes sense on another.
summary: Run the Mailbox Chat relay, review its adapters, and open its command console.

mailboxEndpoint.description: Public registry of agents, connectors, and subscribable mailboxes. Directory only: messages use recipient-cursor semantics (/v1/messages?recipient=), not browsable streams.

servicesEndpoint.description: Workbench enumerator (the relay is a plain http.server with no native endpoint list; this names its proxy mounts).

steps: Install the mailbox_chat package into its own nested .venv (it is a vendored, standalone-only project -- there is no in-process/embedded mode).
Start the standalone relay: mailbox-server.cmd, or `python -m mailbox_chat.server` (the plugin loader also launches it on demand).
Open the command console (/cmd-client) and confirm the configured adapters answer.

plugin-init.description: Redirects /mailbox_chat to the Mailbox Chat relay.

steps: Stop the standalone relay: mailbox-stop.cmd (or terminate the process this plugin's launch() spawned).

This is a vendored nested project (its own .git, its own origin remote) -- remove its directory entirely to uninstall it, or leave it and just disable scanning it (set scan: disabled in plugins.json).

plugin-lifecycle.note: Standalone-only: this is a vendored nested project (its own .git, its own requirements.txt/venv) with no embedded mode. Its 'install' phase is a standalone install (`python -m pip install -e ".[dev]"` in its own directory), and it owns its own process start/stop, so a workbench restart does not restart it -- workbenchShutdown, if implemented, is only a heads-up notification, never a signal to stop or restart the relay.

config.description: Interactive command console (same page as configPage).

restart.description: Exits the relay process so its supervising loop relaunches it with any updated code. Requires the same bearer token as every other authenticated route.

shutdown.description: Exits the relay process and does not relaunch it. Requires the same bearer token as every other authenticated route.

plugin-api.note: restart/shutdown are real routes on the relay's own server (see server.py's do_GET), unlike every other plugin here -- but they stop mailbox_chat's own standalone process, not the embedded workbench API, and are unrelated to the workbenchShutdown lifecycle hook.
